simple.meaning: בַּעַל צְפוֹן (Baʻal Tsᵉphôwn) is a place-name in the Hebrew text (H1189). BibleIQ follows its 3 occurrences across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This place appears in Exodus, Numbers, beginning at Exodus 14:2. The surrounding context includes Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to the Hebrew place-name בַּעַל צְפוֹן (H1189).
simple.whyItMatters: Places in Scripture often connect geography, covenant history, judgment, worship, and movement through the land. BibleIQ keeps the place tied to its actual verse trail.
simple.summary: בַּעַל צְפוֹן (Baʻal Tsᵉphôwn) / H1189 is traced through Exodus 14:2, Exodus 14:9, Numbers 33:7 using generated occurrence evidence.

evidence: Lexicon or morphology identifies this as a proper name

firstOccurrence.englishText: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon. You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

timeline.evidenceText: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon. You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.
The Egyptians pursued them. All the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his army overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baal Zephon.
They traveled from Etham, and turned back to Pihahiroth, which is before Baal Zephon, and they encamped before Migdol.

definitions.full: H1189. Baal Tsephon צְפוֺן בַּ֫עַל proper name, of a location Exod 14:2 , 9 ; Num 33:7 , near Red Sea in Egypt, probably Mt. `Atâka , Eb GS 524 . צְפוֺנִי צְפוֺן, see צִפְיוֺן . below, צְפוֺן , in צְפוֺן בַּעַל (q. v.), perhaps proper name, of deity, Bae Rel. 22 Nö ZMG zlii (1888). 472 Gray Prop. N. 134 .
definitions.rootNote: from 1168 and 6828 (in the sense of cold ) (according to others an Egyptian form of Typhon , the destroyer); Baal of winter ;
